html:
In the early hours of 28 June 1969 police raided the Stonewall Inn, a gay bar in Greenwich Village, New York City. The patrons and a crowd outside fought back, and protests went on for several nights.

Such raids were routine at the time, when gay sex was illegal in almost every state and many lost their jobs if exposed. Among those who resisted were drag queens, lesbians, street youth and trans people.

Within a year new groups such as the Gay Liberation Front had formed, and on the first anniversary marchers held the first Pride parades in New York and other cities. Pride is now held worldwide each June. The Stonewall Inn became a national monument in 2016, after the votes for women and civil rights struggles had set the example.
